reception: Within the sparse-compilation literature the work registers as part of taco's format story. Successor sparse compilers position themselves relative to it: SparseTIR and UniSparse treat the generated conversion routines as a point of departure or a baseline for format customization, and the MLIR sparse-tensor compiler discusses the approach in detail. The work on compiling modular and general sparse workspaces builds on the machinery directly, and papers across sparse linear algebra — from Gamma's sparse matrix multiplication to AlphaSparse's generated SpMV codes — cite the conversion measurements as evidence that format choice and conversion cost matter. The remaining citations are brief mentions in the tensor-compiler literature. The implementation lives on in the tensor-compiler/taco repository, and an evaluated artifact accompanies the paper.
